subject: history_social
passage: Taxila, an ancient city in what is now Pakistan's Punjab province, was a famous center of learning more than 2,000 years ago. Students traveled there from distant regions to study medicine, law, and military skills. Travel guides and websites often call Taxila the world's first university.
passage_b: Historians admire Taxila's teachers but question the label "university." Ancient accounts suggest that students learned from individual teachers in their homes, with no shared campus, set courses, or formal exams. Nalanda, founded centuries later in eastern India, had large shared buildings and organized studies, so it fits the word far better.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the label that travel guides give Taxila in Text 1?

choices.A: By suggesting that students at Taxila studied only medicine
choices.B: By arguing that Taxila's way of teaching does not match what the word suggests
choices.C: By claiming that Nalanda was founded before Taxila became a center of learning
choices.D: By denying that Taxila was an important center of learning

explanation.why: Text 1 reports that travel guides call Taxila "the world's first university." Text 2 "admire[s] Taxila's teachers" but questions the label, because students learned from individual teachers with "no shared campus, set courses, or formal exams." Text 2 says Taxila's teaching did not work like a university.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 1 lists medicine, law, and military skills, and Text 2 never limits the subjects.
explanation.B: Correct. Text 2 says Taxila lacked the campus, courses, and exams that the word "university" suggests.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 says Nalanda was founded "centuries later," not before Taxila.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says historians "admire Taxila's teachers"; it questions only the label.
